denial_reasons: Absence of corticosteroid or hyaluronic acid injection trial: UHC Community Plan policies for knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy (CPT 29881) typically require documented failure of at least one intra-articular injection trial (corticosteroid or viscosupplementation) prior to surgical authorization, unless contraindicated. No injection therapy was administered or contraindication documented.

Insufficient physical therapy duration or visit count: While 8 PT visits over approximately 6 weeks are documented (03/05/2026–04/18/2026), many UHC Community Plan medical necessity criteria require a minimum of 6–8 weeks of formal supervised PT with documented functional outcome measures. The visit count meets the minimum threshold, but the absence of standardized functional outcome scores (KOOS, Lysholm, or equivalent) weakens the demonstration of PT failure.

No formal functional outcome scores documented: UHC and most evidence-based criteria for knee arthroscopy require objective, validated functional outcome measures (e.g., KOOS, Lysholm, IKDC) to quantify baseline impairment and document failure to improve with conservative care. Only VAS pain scores and ROM measurements are present; no KOOS or Lysholm scores were recorded.

Mild chondral changes on MRI may trigger additional scrutiny: The MRI finding of mild medial compartment chondral thinning raises the question of whether the patient's symptoms are attributable to the meniscal tear versus early osteoarthritis. UHC policies may require the submitting physician to explicitly address this distinction and confirm that the primary pain generator is the meniscal tear, not degenerative joint disease.

Mild medial compartment joint space narrowing on X-ray: The 03/01/2026 X-ray finding of mild medial compartment joint space narrowing, in the context of chondral thinning on MRI, may prompt the payer to classify this as a degenerative rather than traumatic meniscal tear, which carries a higher denial risk under UHC's arthroscopy coverage criteria.
